newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen up 15-25 bcf in weekly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen up 15-25 bcf in weekly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to rise by 15 to 25 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations ranged from a draw of 10 bcf to a build of 40 bcf for the week ended November 1. The four-week average build is 56 bcf.
"Based on the weather, it should be a much smaller injection number than last week," said one Houston-based trader, referring to the 34 bcf build in the previous report.
Last week's build was lower than expected and left stocks 256 bcf, or nine percent, below the same year-ago period.
But Eastern stocks at 95 percent of capacity last week looked in good shape ahead of winter, traders said.

Some said relatively mild weather this week and next will result in only minimal draws compared to last year when a cold November forced operators to tap already-low stocks early. Weekly drawdowns in November 1995 averaged 74 bcf, opening the possibility that year-on-year comparisons will show a surplus to last year later in the month if cold weather does not hit.
"Stocks are in pretty good shape, and if we don't see some big drawdowns this month, we could head into December with stocks above last year's levels," said an East Coast trader.
Producing region inventories in the last report continued to seriously lag 1995 levels at just 73 percent full. Stocks in the region last year were at 89 percent of capacity.

For the same week last year, total inventories gained four bcf, meaning a build today in the expected range would narrow the gap to 1995 to about 240 bcf. For the same week in 1995, eastern storage rose by just six bcf, while producing stocks fell by one bcf.
